page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Ecological Adaptations, Succession and Ecological Services · 2 marks

steps.label: Population
lines: Population: a group of individuals of the
SAME species living in a given area at a
Ex: all the mango trees in one orchard.
steps.why: A population is fixed by three things at once — one species, one area, one time. Leaving out any one of them makes the definition incomplete.
common_mistakes: Writing 'a group of plants in an area' without the words same species. That is a community, not a population.
Leaving out the area. A population is always counted for a stated place.
steps.memory_tip: Population = ONE species. Community = MANY species. Count the species.
steps.margin_note: One sentence each. The examiner marks the two definitions separately.

steps.label: Community

lines.text: Community: all the populations in an area

lines: It is the assemblage of the populations of
all the different species living together
Ex: all the plants and animals of a pond.
steps.why: A community is built out of populations, so it is the next level up. Defining it with the word populations shows the examiner the two terms are linked, not separate.
common_mistakes: Defining community as one kind of plant. That is a population.
Adding the soil, water and air. That makes it an ecosystem, not a community.
steps.memory_tip: Levels in order: individual, population, community, ecosystem.
steps.margin_note: Use the word populations inside the community definition — it earns the link mark.

insider_note: The pair is marked as a contrast, so a student who defines both with the same words loses one mark. Put same species in one and all populations in the other.
